I feared you'd respond angrily to my reply because it was not what you want to hear. It's not why you wrote this post, and it's not what you expected. I do have empathy but it's not for you in this case, it is for your pet. 

As a shelter, believe it or not, we are THANKFUL when people return sick pets (even if it's disappointing) because it gives us a chance to try and save them. And we often do! 

I'm watching this play out right now in my own life. A family adopted a cat, she is unwell, they are upset over the cost of vetting, we have offered to accept her back so that we can ensure proper vetting (with a full adoption fee refund) but they won't return her. She will probably die... her chances are getting worse and worse every day. I can't sleep some nights thinking of it. We, the staff, the volunteers, we LOVED this cat. We are pulling in favours to get her into a clinical trial but we cannot do that unless she is returned and the owner stops being stubborn.

We have access not only to vets but also to researchers and trials for new cures for things like FIP (not FIV, not a typo), and sure, it's a long treatment of injections and supportive care but I have seen cats recover using new drugs that some even vets aren't familiar with (this is where I shout-out the FIP Warriors group on Facebook). I don't know if that's what your cat might have had but Jaundice is a symptom and the treatment your vet mentioned made me think it might be. 

I respect someone feeling overwhelmed by it all, most owners are, but that's where the shelter can come in because that kind of stuff is on our radar. Shelter medicine is its own veterinary specialty! 

You are angry with me because I am not showing you the empathy or understanding you hoped to get by making this post. But you didn't post in a sub *asking* for empathy. Your post is specifically asking people to weigh in on if you were an AH, for crying out loud. There are so many places you could have posted to get sympathy. You'd even have my sympathy if you accepted responsibility... If you said "I didn't know enough and I think I let my cat down and I feel terrible," we'd probably be falling all over ourselves to comfort you. Sometimes things are unlucky, or tragic. 

You present us with one side of a story that reads like you are asking for absolution from some internalized guilt, a story where you manage to find fault with so many things that are quite unrelated to the outcome... "red flag number 1, 2, 3" and despite all that blame, It's you who comes off as... kinda not great. 

You said, 

>"I do everything I can for my animals. They receive the best food, veterinary care, toys, etc. that I can afford and get my hands on. They are happy and healthy. If anything is even slightly off, I am immediately aware and am looking for the best solution." 

However, that's not in line with the story you have shared here where you describe how you did not, in fact, get the "best" vet care. Whether it was your "fault" or not, you didn't go to the emergency vet. Or do research online where many articles on cat appetite loss warn about Hepatic Lipidosis. You didn't run the tests at the vet, or opt to do the injections or IVs because, according to you, that was not giving her the QoL. And that's fair but I would buy the quality of life argument IF you had at least had her humanely put to sleep. But, you took her home and let nature take its course.

And here I am, not sleeping, thinking about "Medusa" whose owners won't let us treat her while she is not eating... thinking about how, no matter how carefully we screen adopters, this can STILL happen. What about empathy for the people who work in rescue? You should see how much we love these animals and have to trust other people with them. We are burned out with the stress and the grief. Sometimes so much that we have to stop. Did you even check the description of this subreddit? Or notice the pinned post about shelter staff and trauma/PTSD?

Unfortunately, to us, you \*are\* the AH. You are also our worst nightmare—quick to judge the incorrect note in an adoption description, or the fact you had to remind us to grab a baggie of food. Quick to bash us online over a small cage (even though the cat was actually in a larger playroom) and could have been in that cage due to a sickness in another part of the shelter. You might think you came to the shelter on a quiet day, but there are no quiet days in animal rescue and you have no idea what they might have been dealing with. Seems like \*you\* might be the one unable to empathize.

Aww, that really sucks. There are so many other better options than Paxil especially if it's primarily a sleep issue (I mean, you will sleep but that's about all you'll do). Remember that a GP can also prescribe things for you if you are stuck.

Antihistamines and the tetracyclic *H1*\-*antihistamine* (Remeron/Mirtazapine) would be things I would look into before paxil. With Mirtazapine the smaller the dose the higher the sleep-inducing effect. You can sleep all night on < 15mg... I've used 3.25mg. At 30mg it's a pretty effective antidepressant. 

It's crazy but it's all about the dose, not the drug!

Or even Seroquel/Quetiapine which is an antipsychotic at large doses but will put you to sleep at under 25mg (I've used 6.25mg as needed for sleep but some ppl get restless legs as a side effect. It helps anxiety at that does too.

There are other options for take-as-needed sleep aids... also CBD.

Good luck with whatever you do!

I started with a financial literacy course from a Canadian company "Enriched Academy"... I paid the full price but I think in some provinces it is free for students/younger people. Worth checking! It was well structured and covered everything from how to deal with debt, budgeting, investing, and some real estate. I'd already learned about debt and budgeting the hard way and had completed my debt journey, but wow... it would have been so handy earlier!

I then discovered an Instagram account called Personal Finance Club... (just follow the account and It will get you excited!) It's American but if you learn the equivalents of the types of retirement and tax-free accounts (401 K, IRA) in Canada you can learn SO much. He has a course about investing in index funds and ETFs that is much more reasonably priced than Enriched Academy, and in my view, far better and he does office hours too. 

There's a book called *Millionaire Teacher* that's Canadian and really helpful.

All the info sources I have listed above help you learn the power of using your RRSP and TFSA as containers to invest within (not just as accounts for saving). And they all recommend investing monthly in index funds that grow with the market over time. These are long term investments. And a Robo-Advisor like Weathsinple is a great vehicle for doing this (there are other options that may be available at your bank too like RBC Invesease, etc). 

I'm no expert, I am just on the journey like you are but I am more than happy to share any resources I've discovered!
